report:
Fresh assessment of the complete derive_reflection claim and all one implementation/three test entries. I independently verified exact byte equality of the current sage-reflect implementation/test source and service_spec test source with the supplied historical snapshots; their prior report is context, not the verdict. Current claim requires representation growth through Reflect, no producer hand-serialization of CST/types/signatures/Typed IR, ordinary fields/variants appearing automatically, and documented explicit semantic exceptions. The sole ordinary implementation association exports the derive; its captured whole file defines owned Record/Variant/Sequence/Scalar/Reference output, Reflect::reflected dispatch through default context and finish, and recursive String/Vec reflection. This is meaningful infrastructure but not a universal producer/derive audit.

Both ordinary tests have visible assertions and cfg(test) metadata. derive_preserves_fields derives Example with label and values and asserts both field names, actual String scalar value/type, and Vec type plus two items. derive_preserves_every_enum_payload_shape derives Choice and checks Unit name/empty fields, Tuple name/two fields, and Record name/value field. These catch missing fields and variant-shape losses in these examples; neither establishes every production representation, all nested scalar payloads, all compile forms, or the semantic-override exception. Example/Choice definitions and invoked runtime helpers are in the captured whole-file fragment. I have not treated the exported macro alone as proof of its entire expansion implementation.

The service_spec entry is explicitly TODO (its containing todo module is additionally captured). Its comment defers association and review of complete named/tuple/unit compile/shape evidence, real-product wrappers/nested type trees and continuation boundaries. I accept the existing historical interpretation: the remaining prerequisite is a complete production evidence audit, including producer use of reflection instead of hand serialization and documentation of semantic overrides, followed by associated assertions across those representations. This is unfinished assurance, not implemented universal coverage. The current partial shape tests do not discharge it, and unrelated runtime tests in the whole file are not substituted for its missing associated evidence. There are no N/A entries or TODO implementation entries. All claim aspects are thus accounted for as either concrete partial infrastructure/shape coverage or the retained explicit TODO; no changes to that accounting are requested.

Commands I executed were review start/read, source reads and a Python exact-byte comparison; no behavioral test execution or Rust edits. Coordinator separately reports 321 sage-meta functional tests and cargo build passed; that is not execution performed by this reviewer. All source dependencies used for this limited assessment are in the initial whole implementation/test fragments plus the captured service_spec module context.
